award_layer.source: Copenhagen tourism sources, 2026 list; described as the most starred city in the Nordics
unresolved: A 15-vs-21 gap for 2026 is not rounding. Likely a scope difference (city limits vs greater Copenhagen, or a curated subset vs the full starred list). NOT RESOLVED - do not publish a count.
STARS ARE NOT RESTAURANTS. Never derive a restaurant count from a star count.
Noma has announced a transition away from ordinary restaurant service; its status will change during this project's lifetime. This is why every award entry carries an edition and a date.
For ESPKU the count is irrelevant. What matters is which restaurants are near the venue.
award_layer.ordering_for_october: by distance from the ESPKU venue, not by star count

regime_note: EU Regulation 1169/2011 requires the 14 major allergens to be declared for non-prepacked food including restaurant meals. NINE of the fourteen are phe-relevant protein sources, so for those nine a blank is weak evidence of absence rather than no evidence -- the opposite of the Regime A rule used in Asheville. It says nothing about QUANTITY, so it does not touch the magnitude question.
regime_c_misuse_warnings: Never read an allergen declaration as a quantity. It says whether, never how much.
Never read allergen compliance as accommodation. Declaring milk is a legal duty; cooking without it is a choice.
Legal obligation is not compliance. Treating Regime C silence as STRONG evidence is the same overreach as treating Regime A silence as evidence, in the opposite direction.
Confidence still decays with snapshot age. Regime C does not exempt a menu from recency rules.

blocking_gate.blocked_until: the lexicon has a Danish category set
blocking_gate.why: The lexicon is English-first. A Danish menu run through it today would match ~nothing and the census would record 'no protein sources named', which is the worst possible failure of the one inference rule -- a tooling gap presented as a finding about food.
known_hard_problems: Danish compounds aggressively: 'svinekødsfrikadeller' is one word containing pork AND meatball. The compound_substring_terms pass was built for 'shrimpburger' and needs real work.
Non-ASCII: ae/oe/aa characters will break naive matching. slugify() folds them; the lexicon matcher does not. This is a bug waiting to happen.
The seed term list above is the agent's, not a native speaker's. It will contain errors and will miss the compounds that matter most.

green_star_note: Copenhagen is dense with Green Stars (Geranium, Noma). A Green Star is awarded for sustainability. Vegetable-forward correlates with it, which is a CAMOUFLAGE signal, never a dietary-fit signal. Sustainable cooking often displaces meat with legumes, which are among the highest-phe foods. See PRIORS.md prior 5.

october_scope: order the Michelin list BY DISTANCE from the venue and delegate hotels, then work down
capture menus by any means including hand transcription
the request card in Danish, translated by a person, not a machine
nothing else - no scoring, no lexicon rollout, no verification campaign
event_anchor.why_bib_over_stars: A Bib Gourmand is Michelin's good-value tier, which correlates with a la carte service and a printed menu. Both are better for a delegate than a prepaid tasting menu. The starred set is the more prestigious list and the less useful one for this trip.
event_anchor.opportunity: A few hundred PKU families eating in one city in one week. A structured visit report form would be the largest accommodation dataset this project has ever had, and it also tests the tasting-menu prediction in PRIORS.md with a sample no amount of scraping produces. Worth designing the form before October even if nothing else ships.
